title: Impersonal and causative passives
titleVi: Bị động khách quan và bị động nhờ vả
summary: Hai cấu trúc bị động đưa band lên 8.0: người ta nói rằng (it is said that) và nhờ người khác làm (have something done).
whyItMatters: Đây là hai cấu trúc đặc trưng của văn phong học thuật band 8.0. *It is widely believed that* giúp bạn nêu quan điểm chung mà không quy cho ai, còn *have something done* nén cả một câu dài thành bốn từ. Không dùng được chúng, bài viết của bạn vẫn đúng ngữ pháp nhưng nghe rất giống văn nói.

sections.heading: Two ways to report what people say
body: When you report an opinion without naming who holds it, English offers two impersonal passive patterns. The **it**-pattern keeps a full clause: *It is widely believed that remote work raises productivity.* The **subject**-pattern promotes the person or thing to subject and turns the verb into a to-infinitive: *Remote work is widely believed to raise productivity.*

Both patterns exist because academic writing prefers to present a claim as shared knowledge rather than personal opinion. The verb set is small and formal: **allege, believe, consider, estimate, expect, know, report, say, suppose, think, understand**.

The choice between them is partly rhythm. The **it**-pattern is better when the clause is long or already contains a that-clause; the **subject**-pattern gives you a short, punchy sentence and reads slightly more confident.

rows: It is said that the drug reduces symptoms.
The drug is said to reduce symptoms.
It is thought that the two events are linked.
The two events are thought to be linked.
It is expected that prices will fall.
It is understood that the talks have failed.
The talks are understood to have failed.

sections.heading: Matching the infinitive to the time of the claim
body: The to-infinitive carries its own time reference. If the claim concerns the present or a general truth, use **to do** or **to be doing**. If it concerns something earlier than the reporting verb, use **to have done**.

Passive claims stack two passives: *He is said to have been arrested* means people say that he was arrested. Keep the order **to have been + past participle**; do not fall back on *to be arrested* when the arrest is clearly in the past.
The same logic applies to states: *The building is thought to be unsafe* (now) versus *The building is thought to have been unsafe* (at the time of the fire).

examples.right: The company is reported to be losing millions.
examples.wrong: The company is reported to lose millions.
examples.note: An ongoing situation takes **to be + -ing**, not the simple infinitive.

examples.right: She is believed to have left the country in March.
The manuscript is said to have been written in the twelfth century.
examples.note: Earlier event plus passive → **to have been + past participle**.

sections.heading: Fixed frames: there is said to be, supposed to
body: **There is said to be** replaces *People say there is*: *There is said to be a link between the two phenomena.* The frame is fixed, so the verb agrees with the following noun: *There are said to be dozens of cases.*

**be supposed to** carries three different meanings, and examiners notice when a candidate can use only one. It can report general belief: *The film is supposed to be excellent.* It can report an arrangement or expectation: *You were supposed to be here at nine.* And in the negative it reports prohibition: *You are not supposed to park here.*
For an expectation that was not fulfilled, add the perfect infinitive: *The train was supposed to have arrived an hour ago.*

examples.right: The monument is supposed to be the oldest in the region.
The assignment is supposed to have been submitted last Friday.
Passengers are not supposed to use mobile phones during take-off.

sections.heading: have something done: getting someone else to act
body: The causative **have/get + object + past participle** says that you arranged for another person to do something: *We had the data analysed by an independent statistician.* The object is what receives the action; the doer, if you mention it, follows **by**.

The pattern works in every tense because only **have** changes: *I'm having my eyes tested*, *She had her appendix removed*, *They will have the site inspected*. Questions and negatives use ordinary do-support: *Did you have your hair cut?*

**get** is more informal and more common in speech: *I got my laptop repaired.* Do not confuse the causative with the past perfect — *I had repaired my laptop* means I did it myself, *I had my laptop repaired* means someone else did it.

rows: She had translated the report herself.

sections.heading: The misfortune meaning — and how to use it precisely
body: The same form reports an unwelcome event that someone experienced: *The team had their funding cut.* Nothing was arranged; the subject is a victim. Context, not grammar, separates the two meanings, so keep the doer clear: *They had their bags stolen* (victim) versus *They had their bags searched* (arranged, usually by officials).

In IELTS Writing the causative is a compact way to describe policy: *Cities should have older buildings retrofitted rather than demolished.* It also removes the clumsy *someone does something for somebody* that appears in so many band-6 essays.
Keep the object and the participle adjacent. Long objects read badly: *They had the house that they bought last year painted* is grammatical but heavy — split it into two sentences.

examples.right: The council had the unsafe bridge closed to traffic.
examples.note: Arranged action: officials caused the closure.

examples.right: Several families had their homes flooded after the storm.
examples.note: Misfortune: they did not arrange anything.

examples.right: You should have your thesis proofread before submission.
examples.note: Causative in a modal frame — very common advice in academic contexts.

commonMistakes.wrong: He is said that he has moved to Da Nang.
commonMistakes.right: He is said to have moved to Da Nang.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt giữ nguyên cả mệnh đề sau *nói* (*Người ta nói rằng anh ấy đã chuyển...*), nên người học giữ luôn *that*. Khi đã đưa chủ ngữ lên đầu, tiếng Anh bắt buộc dùng **to + động từ**, không dùng mệnh đề.

commonMistakes.wrong: The company is believed to fire 200 workers last year.
commonMistakes.right: The company is believed to have fired 200 workers last year.
commonMistakes.why: Hành động xảy ra trước động từ tường thuật phải dùng **to have + V3**. Tiếng Việt không chia thì trong động từ nguyên mẫu nên lỗi này gần như vô hình với người học.

commonMistakes.wrong: I had repaired my motorbike at the shop yesterday.
commonMistakes.right: I had my motorbike repaired at the shop yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: *Nhờ* ai làm gì phải dùng **have + tân ngữ + V3**. Thiếu tân ngữ và quá khứ phân từ, câu chuyển sang nghĩa tự tay bạn sửa xe — điều bạn không hề muốn nói.

commonMistakes.wrong: She got cleaned her apartment before the guests arrived.
commonMistakes.right: She got her apartment cleaned before the guests arrived.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt đặt động từ ngay sau *nhờ/lấy* (*nhờ dọn căn hộ*), còn tiếng Anh cố định khung **have/get + tân ngữ + V3**. Đảo trật tự là lỗi ngữ pháp, không phải lỗi văn phong.

commonMistakes.wrong: The building is said to be damaged in the storm.
commonMistakes.right: The building is said to have been damaged in the storm.
commonMistakes.why: Vừa bị động vừa chỉ thời gian trước, nên cần **to have been + V3**. Người học dừng ở *to be damaged* vì *bị hư hại* trong tiếng Việt trông giống một trạng thái hơn là một hành động đã xảy ra.

ieltsTips: Mở một đoạn thân bài Task 2 bằng bị động khách quan để nêu quan điểm chung, rồi tự nhận trách nhiệm ở câu sau: *It is widely argued that...* ... *This essay contends that...*
Dùng `is said to` và `is thought to` khi trích một nhận định bạn không kiểm chứng được — cách nói thận trọng này được đánh giá cao hơn *people say* ở band 7.5+.
Trong Task 1 mô tả quy trình, hãy dùng bị động thường (*the mixture is heated*) chứ không dùng cấu trúc nhờ vả; `have something done` để dành cho con người và chính sách trong Task 2.
Thay `people say` bằng `it is often claimed that` ngay ở mở bài: chỉ thêm ba từ nhưng câu văn lập tức đọc ra chất C1.

exercises.question: The new stadium ___ to have cost more than two billion dollars.
exercises.explanation: Cấu trúc **subject + be + believed + to have done** cho một sự việc đã xảy ra trong quá khứ.

exercises.question: ___ that the two countries will sign the treaty this week.
exercises.explanation: Mẫu **It is expected that + mệnh đề** là bị động khách quan; *it* không phải chủ ngữ hành động nên không chia chủ động.

exercises.question: We ___ the kitchen redecorated while we were away on holiday.
exercises.explanation: **have + tân ngữ + V3** diễn tả việc nhờ người khác làm; *make/let* đi với động từ nguyên mẫu, không đi với quá khứ phân từ.

exercises.question: Which sentence means that someone else cut his hair?
exercises.explanation: Chỉ **had his hair cut** (have + tân ngữ + V3) mới mang nghĩa nhờ người khác cắt; *had cut* là thì quá khứ hoàn thành.

exercises.question: The witness ___ to have left the country before the trial began.
exercises.explanation: **is alleged to have left** = người ta cáo buộc rằng nhân chứng đã rời đi; *allege* ở đây phải là bị động khách quan.

exercises.question: The minister ___ (report) to be considering a change in policy.
exercises.explanation: Hiện tại, đang diễn ra → **is reported to be considering**.

exercises.question: The painting ___ (believe) to have been stolen in 1998.
exercises.explanation: Niềm tin hiện tại về một sự việc quá khứ: **is believed to have been stolen**.

exercises.question: I must have my eyes ___ (test) before I renew my driving licence.
exercises.explanation: Khung nhờ vả cần quá khứ phân từ: **have my eyes tested**.

exercises.question: They ___ their car stolen while they were staying in Da Lat.
exercises.explanation: Nghĩa *bị* tai họa: **had their car stolen**, không phải *stole*.

exercises.question: There ___ (say) to be a serious shortage of skilled workers.
exercises.explanation: Khung cố định **There is said to be + cụm danh từ số ít**, tương đương *People say there is...*.
